# Ordinary Bits transport first-source experiment

[Session](session.json) preserves eight complete desired projects before
implementation and 36 actual CLI observations. First sources remain unchanged;
[assessment](assessment.json) distinguishes three observer syntax/import repairs
from actual ordinary-register profile refusals. Current repaired projects are in
attempt-02, except generic-one and measured-copy in attempt-03.

[Independent intended distributions](expectations.json) retain the four ordered
two-bit rows, empty register copying, nested products and Bell-correlated readout.
None was produced by this baseline: selected Raw rejects ordinary Bits, while
finite project execution rejects registers or the separate static-Nat profile.
These refusals establish no downstream semantic/ownership rule. First two
captures retain structured JSON diagnostics, not byte-exact stdout formatting;
the third also retains raw stdout. Binary identities are checked before/after.

The following implementation must preserve exact source types and independently
replay the actual accepted artifact; native IR validity alone is insufficient.
This is informed design/diagnostic evidence for bug #342 and #32/#250/#44, not a
blind author benchmark, implementation completion, new guarantee or proof.
